title: Speaking Clubs
description: Topic-driven discussion sessions with handcrafted vocabulary, level calibration (A2–C1), and structured speaking rounds.

clubs.title: I Couldn't Help But Wonder
clubs.description: Curious reflections, personal dilemmas, and observational discussion topics inspired by modern life.

prompts.text: What is a small habit you noticed in others that you find interesting or strange?
Have you ever wondered why people find it hard to say 'no' to invitations?
How do digital communication tools change the way we maintain long-term friendships?
To what extent does social expectation shape our personal definitions of success?

clubs.title: Keeping Up with Science
clubs.description: Debates and explorations around modern scientific discoveries, technology, and environmental issues.

prompts.text: What piece of technology do you use every day that you couldn't live without?
How will artificial intelligence change everyday jobs in the next ten years?
What measures should cities prioritize to combat urban pollution and climate change?
Should genetic engineering in medicine be strictly regulated by international law?

clubs.title: Mind Matters
clubs.description: Engaging conversations on psychology, emotional intelligence, habits, and mental well-being.

prompts.text: What is one healthy habit you would like to develop this year?
How do you usually relax after a very stressful day or week?
In what ways does cognitive bias influence our daily decision-making processes?
How can modern society balance productivity demands with mental health preservation?

clubs.title: Debatable & Relatable
clubs.description: Lighthearted yet thought-provoking debates on common daily dilemmas and light controversial topics.

prompts.text: Is it better to live in a quiet countryside town or a bustling big city?
Should companies mandate a four-day work week for all full-time employees?
Is remote working overall more beneficial or detrimental to team culture and collaboration?
Does public shaming on social media ever serve a legitimate moral purpose?

clubs.title: Let's Celebrate
clubs.description: Cultural traditions, festivities, milestones, and shared cultural celebrations across the world.

prompts.text: What is your favorite holiday or annual celebration, and how do you celebrate it?
How have traditional family celebrations evolved in your country over the past decade?
Why do humans across all cultures feel a strong need to mark seasonal milestones with festivals?
Has the commercialization of global holidays weakened their underlying cultural significance?

clubs.title: My Life With/Without
clubs.description: Personal storytelling and reflection on living with or without specific items, habits, or circumstances.

prompts.text: How would your weekend change if you spent it completely without smartphone or internet access?
Could you comfortably live in a minimal home with only 100 personal possessions?
How has living with or without pets/hobbies shaped your personal growth?
To what extent do physical possessions contribute to long-term psychological fulfillment?

clubs.title: The Greatest Quotes
clubs.description: Inspiring quotes, proverbs, and philosophical sayings evaluated and debated by participants.

prompts.text: What does 'Practice makes perfect' mean to you in your language learning journey?
Discuss the quote: 'The journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.'
Debate the famous statement: 'Fortune favors the bold.' Is caution sometimes wiser?
Analyze Nietzsche's assertion: 'He who has a why to live can bear almost any how.'

clubs.title: If You Were
clubs.description: Hypothetical role-play scenarios and imaginative prompt decks to unlock fluid expression across speculative situations.

prompts.text: If you were the mayor of your city for one day, what single rule or law would you create?
If you were a world-renowned artist, musician, or writer, what kind of work would you produce?
If you were transported to live in any historical century, which era would you choose and why?
If you were appointed leader of an interplanetary human colony, how would you structure its initial government?
